question: Should plugin approval cancellation be standardized as `plugin.approval.resolved` with `decision: null`, or should cancellation use a separate event/API before this PR proceeds?
rationale: The PR's code direction is plausible, but it creates a public gateway/plugin SDK contract that affects bundled and third-party approval consumers; automation should not choose that permanent API shape alone.

options.title: Accept nullable resolved cleanup
options.body: Keep `decision: null` as the cancellation/timeout cleanup signal, then require sibling requester coverage, docs, SDK/consumer tests, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Use a separate cancellation contract
options.body: Ask the branch to replace nullable resolved decisions with a distinct cancel/remove event or API so resolved decisions remain non-null.

options.title: Land only the narrow requester fix
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally scope this PR to before_tool_call only, but the linked issue should remain open for the uncovered requester paths.

recommendation.title: Accept nullable resolved cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep `decision: null` as the cancellation/timeout cleanup signal, then require sibling requester coverage, docs, SDK/consumer tests, and real behavior proof before merge.
